t: whether a positive or a negative commandment. The former are those that command doing something, the latter those that command refraining from an act.
whether intentionally or unintentionally. Deliberately or by mistake.
when he repents and turns from his sin. When he decides to return to God from now on, and regrets what he has already sinned.
and this confession is a positive commandment. See Sefer ha-Mitzvot, positive commandment 73.
I have sinned, I have done wrong, I have transgressed before You. I understand that the act I did is a sin, a wrong, and a transgression.
and behold, I regret and am ashamed of my deeds. I regret this act and am ashamed of it.
and I will never return to this thing. I commit never to do this again.
one who confesses at length and elaborates on this matter. One who spells out his intention in each of the stages described.

those obligated to bring sin-offerings and guilt-offerings. Those who committed a transgression for which a sin-offering or guilt-offering is required (for details see Hilchot Shegagot 1:2, 8:1, 9:1).
at the time they bring their offerings. The confession is said at the time one leans on the offering before it is brought (Hilchot Ma'aseh ha-Korbanot 3:14-15).
they do not receive atonement through their offering, etc.. For if he did not fully regret his actions, the offering is of no avail (and see Hilchot Shegagot 3:10).

they do not receive atonement through their death or their lashes. For punishments atone for the offenders (see Hilchot Sanhedrin 13:1, 17:7), but this is on condition that they repented (and see below, halakhah 4).
even though he paid him what he owed him. In return for what he damaged him in person or in property.
from all the sins of man. This includes all sins between a person and his fellow, for whose full atonement confession is required (compare Hilchot Chovel 5:9-10).
the scapegoat. Brought on Yom Kippur to atone for the sins of Israel (Hilchot Avodat Yom ha-Kippurim 3:1-7).

in the name of all Israel. On behalf of all Israel: "Please, O Lord, Your people the house of Israel have sinned, done wrong and transgressed before You. Please, O Lord, grant atonement for the sins, wrongs and transgressions that Your people the house of Israel have sinned, done wrong and transgressed before You..." (Hilchot Avodat Yom ha-Kippurim 4:2).
whether it was made known to him or not made known to him. Whether he knows that he committed a transgression, or does not know exactly what he did (see Hilchot Shegagot 8:1, 11:9).
karet. Being cut off of the soul from the World to Come (see below 8:1).

and a false or vain oath... is among the severe ones. For it says of it, "The Lord will not hold guiltless one who takes His name in vain" (Exodus 20:7, Deuteronomy 5:11), and it involves desecration of God's name (Hilchot Shevu'ot 12:1-2; and see below, halakhah 4, Hilchot Yesodei ha-Torah 5:10).
and we have no altar of atonement. For it is not possible to bring a sin-offering or guilt-offering.
there is only repentance. The matter depends on repentance without an offering.
in the end. At the end of his life.
and the essence of Yom Kippur itself atones for those who repent. Even without the scapegoat.
at the time. Immediately.
Return, backsliding children, and I will heal your backslidings. If you repent, I will immediately forgive you for your wayward deeds.
repentance suspends. It leaves his judgment undecided, for merit or for guilt.
and the sufferings that come upon him complete the atonement for him. They complete the atonement.
I will punish their transgression with the rod and their iniquity with plagues. For there are sins and transgressions that are forgiven only through pain and suffering.
but one who desecrates the Name. For example, one who deliberately transgressed to spite God (Hilchot Yesodei ha-Torah 5:10, and see there in the chapter for more examples).

and the Lord of Hosts revealed Himself in my ears: This iniquity shall not be atoned for you until you die. For the atonement of the most severe transgressions is completed only with the death of the sinner.
one to whom there came a matter in which he had sinned. That is, an opportunity presented itself to him to commit a transgression under the same conditions in which he had committed it in the past.
and he separated and did not do it because of repentance. He overcame his inclination and did not transgress a second time, because of his decision to repent.
and remember your Creator in the days of your youth. Remember the Creator while you are young, and repent before you reach old age, when repentance is not as excellent, as explained below.
and at a time when he can no longer do what he used to do. That is, because of the weakness of his body.
it avails him. The repentance is accepted and effective.
on the day of his death. On the last day of his life.
before the sun grows dark. A metaphor for the end of a person's life.
that the sinner abandon his sin. That he cease committing the transgression.
he regrets. He is remorseful.

after I returned I regretted, and after I was made to know I struck my thigh. After I turned back from the sin and its gravity became known to me, I regretted it and behaved in a way that expresses sorrow.
He who knows hidden things. God Himself, who knows thoughts.
in You the orphan finds mercy. One can rely only on God, who has mercy on orphans.
and he must confess with his lips and say these matters that he resolved in his heart. Above 1:1.
and did not resolve in his heart to abandon. That is, he did not truly decide to abandon the sin in the future.
like one who immerses while holding a creeping creature in his hand. For although he immerses to become pure, the creeping creature still defiles him.
and whoever confesses and abandons will find mercy. For confessing the sin is not enough; one must abandon it.
this people has sinned a great sin and made themselves a god of gold. Said after the sin of the golden calf, and the nature of the sin was spelled out in the confession.
among the ways of repentance. The patterns of conduct that characterize complete repentance (see also Hilchot Ta'aniyot 1:2).
cries out constantly before the Lord. Prays for forgiveness.
and gives charity according to his ability. According to his means (see Hilchot Matnot Aniyim 7:5), as atonement for his deeds.
that is, I am a different person, etc.. As an expression that he is not the same person who sinned.
for exile atones for sin. See Hilchot Rotze'ach 7:13.
that he confess in public. Thereby he gives additional force to his confession and his commitment.
indeed. Truly.
and whoever is proud and does not make known. One who refrains from admitting his failure in public out of self-respect.
for transgressions between a person and his fellow. For this helps to appease the other.
that are between him and God. In commandments between a person and the Holy One, blessed be He, that do not affect others.
and it is brazenness on his part if he reveals them. For publicizing transgressions of this kind involves desecration of God's name.
in general terms. Without specifying the sin, saying only "I have sinned."
seek the Lord when He can be found, call upon Him when He is near. For in these days God is near, and they are therefore days of favor suited for repentance.
whenever they repent. For the Holy One, blessed be He, does not reject the prayer of the many (Hilchot Tefillah 8:1).
as the Lord our God whenever we call to Him. At any time that we call to Him.
and it is the end of pardon and forgiveness for Israel. A fixed time in the year for pardon and forgiveness (Ma'aseh Rokeach).
from the eve of the day. Before Yom Kippur begins.
before he eats. Before the final meal before the fast.
lest he choke during the meal. While eating the meal.
after his prayer. At the end of the Amidah prayer.
but we have sinned, etc.. Indeed, we have sinned (for the full text see Seder ha-Tefillot, 59).
and it is the essence of the confession. Its core (see above 1:1).
for I know my transgressions, and my sin is always before me. I always remember my sins, and they give me no rest.
and appease him. Pacify him (and see above 1:1).
and to entreat. To plead.
a row of three of his friends. A delegation of friends to appease the friend.
rather he should be easily appeased and hard to anger. Easy to pacify, and not easily angered.
troubled him. Harassed him.
he shall not take revenge or bear a grudge. He should not harm another because the other harmed him, nor remember the harm done to him (see Hilchot De'ot 7:7-8).
the uncircumcised of heart. Those whose hearts are closed.
and his wrath he kept forever. The anger is remembered forever.
and the Gibeonites were not of the children of Israel. The fact that they did not forgive proves that they are not of the children of Israel (and see further Hilchot Issurei Bi'ah 12:24, 19:17).
he brings ten people and stands them at his grave. So that this is part of asking for forgiveness and confessing in public (as above, halakhah 5).
let him leave it with the court. As a deposit in their hands until the heirs are found, in order to fulfill the return of the debt (see Hilchot Gezelah 7:10).
half and half. His sins and his merits are evenly balanced against each other, with no decisive tilt between them.
and so the whole world. It is judged according to the deeds of all its inhabitants.
a person whose sins outweigh his merits. Whose sins are so many that there is grounds to judge him immediately (for the regular judgment see below, halakhah 3).

because of the multitude of your iniquity. "For I have struck you as an enemy strikes, with cruel chastisement, because of the multitude of your iniquity, because your sins were many." And in the verse after it: "Why do you cry over your wound? Your pain is incurable. Because of the multitude of your iniquity, because your sins were many, I have done these things to you."
the outcry of Sodom and Gomorrah, for it is great, etc.. For the cities of Sodom sinned greatly and their sentence was decreed, that they be overturned.
and the Lord saw that the wickedness of man was great. Said before the decree to destroy the world in the flood in the days of Noah.
the count of merits and sins. Their total number.
because there was found in him something good. Said of the son of Jeroboam, who was saved by one good deed he did from the sentence of destruction decreed on all his family.
and one sinner destroys much good. For there are sins that may cause the loss of many merits.
by the knowledge of the God of knowledge. For He alone knows the weight of deeds one against the other.
who regretted... and wondered. Regretted.
perhaps I had not done them. If only I had not done them.
and they are not mentioned. They are not taken into account.
as one who wonders about his earlier deeds. Who regrets his earlier deeds.

just as a person's sins and merits are weighed at the time of his death. In order to decree his judgment after his death, and also to decide whether he has a share in the World to Come (see below, halakhot 5-6).
on the festival of Rosh Hashanah. On which people are judged for life in the new year.
they suspend it for him. They wait to decide his judgment.

even though the sounding of the shofar on Rosh Hashanah is a decree of Scripture. Although we fulfill the commandment only because the Torah so commanded, it is nevertheless proper to find a reason and purpose for it (see also Hilchot Me'ilah 8:8, Hilchot Temurah 4:13).
there is a hint in it, as if to say, Awake, etc.. The sounding of the shofar expresses a call to repent.
those who forget the truth in the vanities of time. Who turn to passing things.
therefore every person must, etc.. Since the world is judged each Rosh Hashanah according to people's deeds, each person must see himself as if the responsibility rests on him alone.
to increase in charity and good deeds and to engage in mitzvot... more than all the days of the year. In order to tip the world toward merit during the days of judgment.
the first sin. The first time.
those two sins combine. In the weighing of sins, because he is found to be unworthy of this kindness of forgiving the first sins.
they pass over all his sins one after another. They forgive them one after the other.
if he was among the half of sins that include that he never put on tefillin. That is a grave sin, and he is considered a transgressor of Israel with his body.
they judge him according to his sins. And they do not forgive "one after another."
and he has a share in the World to Come. As part of all Israel, even though he sinned.
this land is a metaphor. It is not speaking of "land" in its literal sense (see below 8:7).
the pious of the nations of the world. Gentiles who keep the seven Noahide commandments and accepted them upon themselves because the Holy One, blessed be He, commanded them (Hilchot Melakhim 8:11).
are cut off and destroyed. Their soul is cut off from the World to Come and perishes like the soul of an animal (below 8:1).
and are judged... forever and ever. With suffering over their being cut off from life.
the heretics, the epicureans, and those who deny the Torah. These names will be explained below in halakhot 7-13 (and see also Hilchot Edut 11:10).
and those who deny the coming of the redeemer. Who is also considered one who denies the Torah (Hilchot Melakhim 11:1).
and slanderers. Those who speak ill of others (Hilchot De'ot 7:2-3).
and one who draws forward his foreskin. So that he appears uncircumcised (see Hilchot Milah 3:8).
five are called heretics, etc.. All of these deny the foundations of knowing God explained in Hilchot Yesodei ha-Torah, chapter 1.
that He is a body and has a form. A tangible image.
that He alone is not first and the rock of all. That He is not the source of everything, but rather there were materials before Him that He used to create the world.

and likewise one who worships a god other than Him, etc.. An angel or a person or one of the forces of nature, who holds that it has the power to act as an intermediary (see Hilchot Avodah Zarah 1:1, 2:1).
epicureans. Those who deny the connection between the Creator and creatures (and see Hilchot Avodah Zarah 2:5).
if Moses said it on his own. From his own words, and not from the mouth of God.
and denies its transmitters, such as Zadok and Boethus. One who challenges the tradition and authority of the Sages of the Oral Torah, as Zadok and Boethus did.
and the Hagrites. Muslims.
who has made it his habit. Who does so as a regular practice.
to wear shatnez. A garment of mixed wool and linen (Hilchot Kil'ayim, chapter 10).
to round off the corners of the head. To shave the sidelocks of the head (Hilchot Avodah Zarah 12:1-2).
such as one who returns to the religions of the gentiles. Who converted to another religion (and for further cases see Hilchot Avodah Zarah 2:5).
who decree forced conversion. A death decree for observing the commandments.
like Jeroboam. Who caused Israel to sin by the worship of golden calves (II Kings 12:28).
and Zadok and Boethus. Who denied the authority and tradition of the Sages.
a positive commandment. One considered a minor commandment (see above 1:4).
like Jesus. Jesus the Christian, who led Israel into idolatry.
one who separates himself from the ways of the community. He does not consider himself part of the community of Israel (compare Hilchot Evel 1:10).
separated. Apart.
and does not perform mitzvot along with them. Together with the congregation.
with a high hand, like Jehoiakim. Who acted insolently toward the words of the Torah (see Jeremiah chapter 36).
brazenly. Acts insolently.
such as the kings of the nations. He acts like the kings of the nations.
even though they are Israel. Of the seed of Israel, regarding whom the rule is that all have a share in the World to Come (above, halakhah 5).
and nevertheless, etc.. Although these are light compared with the transgressions listed before, the Sages warned that one who commits them has lost his share in the World to Come.
one who calls his fellow by a nickname. A nickname that carries disgrace.
and one who shames his fellow. Embarrasses him (Hilchot De'ot 6:8).

and one who elevates himself through the disgrace of his fellow. He lists his own good deeds and wisdom against those of his fellow, so that it appears from the comparison that he is honored and his fellow is despised (below 4:4, Hilchot De'ot 6:3).
and one who despises Torah scholars. Hilchot Talmud Torah 6:11.
and one who despises the festivals. Who does not honor the holidays but treats them like weekdays (Hilchot Yom Tov 6:16).
and one who profanes sacred things. Offerings and things that were consecrated to the Temple.
turned from his wickedness. Regretted his deeds.
Peace, peace to the far and to the near, says the Lord, and I will heal him. For even one who was far has a remedy and a cure (see above 1:3, 2:1).
in secret places. In private, while in public they behave as before.
for he is still wayward. And does not behave entirely properly.
we accept him in repentance. See Hilchot Avodah Zarah 2:5 and the commentary there.
hinder repentance. Make it difficult for a person to repent.
a great sin. For the gravity of the sin is so great that he is punished by not having the chance to repent.
one who causes the many to sin, etc.. Above 3:10.
such as one who entices and leads astray. Who entice to idolatry (Hilchot Avodah Zarah, chapter 4, and 5:1-5).
in a bad upbringing. Raised in a bad way.
since his son is under his authority. He has influence over him.
was turning away. Leaving his evil deeds.
whoever is able to protest to others. And they would accept his rebuke (see Hilchot De'ot 6:7).
I will sin and repent, etc.. He grants himself permission to sin because he relies on being forgiven when he repents or on Yom Kippur.
lock the paths of repentance. Make it hard to return in repentance, and the reason will be explained in each of the items.
one who separates from the community. Does not take part with the community (above 3:10).
and does not share with them in the merits they earn. He does not join them in the commandments they perform when they return in repentance.
and does not know the ways of repentance. For he does not learn from the Sages.
does not pursue them. Does not strive to perform them properly.
will gain merit. Will gain merit for himself.
causes them to push him away and drive him off, like Jesus and Gehazi. Until in the end they left the way of the Torah.
and they shame him. They embarrass him.
remember, do not forget... you have been rebellious. Moses our teacher's rebuke of Israel for their sins in the wilderness.
but the Lord has not given you a heart. That is, they did not understand from the miracles that happened to them in the wilderness that God watches over them.
a foolish people and not wise. In the Song of Ha'azinu, in astonishment that Israel corrupts its ways, He called them this.
Ah, sinful nation. A people of sinners.
the ox knows its owner. The ox knows who its owner is, but "Israel does not know."
for I know that you are stubborn. I know that you are stiff-necked.
cry aloud, do not hold back. Shout in a loud voice.
to appoint. To designate (and see Hilchot Ta'aniyot 4:2).
therefore he will remain in his sins, which are good in his eyes. He will continue his evil deeds, since there is no possibility that he will awaken to examine their nature.
it is impossible for him to repent completely, etc.. For with sins between a person and his fellow, he is not forgiven until he gives his fellow what he owes him and appeases him (above 2:9).
and one who shares with the thief. Who divides the loot with him, or buys from him (see Hilchot Genevah 5:1, Hilchot Gezelah 5:1).
for he strengthens the hand of the thief. By buying from him what he stole, he causes him to continue stealing.
and does not announce it until he returns it to its owner. He does not publicize the found item, and the owners despair of searching for it (see Hilchot Gezelah va-Avedah 11:2).
and one who eats the plunder of the poor, orphans and widows. Property that was robbed from them.
and they have no acquaintance who would know whose plunder this is and return it to him. Because they wander and are not known, it is impossible to return to them what was taken from them.

for the matter has legs. There is a high probability that the bribe swayed the judge's opinion. Since there is no way to estimate how far his opinion was swayed, he cannot know how much he must return to those who lost in his rulings.
for he strengthens the hand of this one. The one who gives the bribe, causing him to continue this conduct.
it is not presumed that they will turn from them. The assumption is that he will not turn from them.
light matters. Which are not perceived as transgressions.
from a meal that is not enough for its owner. A poor man whom he invited to eat with him, and the meal is not sufficient for the host himself.
a trace of robbery. A sort of prohibition of robbery, for the host did not intend that this person eat at his home, but only invited him as a polite gesture.
in his pledge. A vessel he placed as security for a loan.
and says in his heart, They are not diminished, and I did not rob him. And he does not pay him for the use of the vessels, or deduct it from the loan.
and one who looks at forbidden relations. At women forbidden as ervah (see Hilchot Issurei Bi'ah 21:2-3).
and you shall not go about after your own heart. "...and after your own eyes," for following the desire of the heart and the sight of the eyes eventually leads to an actual transgression.

for his fellow is not standing there, and no shame came to him and he did not shame him. He did not explicitly say anything disgraceful about him; rather the matter emerges from the comparison (see Hilchot De'ot 6:3).
and one who suspects the upright. Suspects them of having done something improper.
gossip and slander. Speech about the deeds of others (see Hilchot De'ot 7:1-6).
and one prone to anger. Their anger (ibid. 2:3).
and one with an evil thought. For example, thoughts of deceit or lust (see ibid. 2:6-7).
for he learns from his deeds and they are imprinted on his heart. And in the end he behaves like the wicked person (see ibid. 6:1-2).
all the more so for a penitent. Who must be more careful in his deeds (and see ibid. 2:1-2).
he will be drawn after them constantly. And will be unable to stop his habit.
to separate. To keep apart.
exceedingly evil traits. Bad character traits.
do not prevent repentance. Despite what is said in this chapter, repentance for these transgressions is possible, with great effort (and see above 3:14).
every person's free will is given to him. Every person has the ability to choose.
to incline himself. To direct his path.
the choice is in his hand. He is given the ability to do so.
this is what is written in the Torah. In the Genesis story, after Adam and Eve ate from the Tree of Knowledge.
was unique in the world. A unique species in the world ("has become like one").
he, on his own, by his knowledge and thought, knows good and evil. That on his own he can decide whether to do good or evil ("from himself, to know good and evil").
that would hold him back. That would prevent him.
lest he stretch out his hand. Man was expelled from the Garden of Eden, out of concern that he might choose to stretch out his hand to the Tree of Life, and then "eat and live forever."
a miser or a generous man. Stingy or generous.
he has destroyed himself. By choosing sin.
why should a living man complain, a man for his sins. It is proper to be sorry and to lament one's sins, for they are solely the sinner's fault.
and He went on to say. In the following verse.
let us search and examine our ways and return to the Lord. After understanding that our path is our responsibility, one can decide to repent.
the pillar of the Torah and the commandment. The Torah and the commandments are based on it.
that is, the choice is in your hands. That one can choose between life, good and blessing, and death, evil and curse.

it is said, Who will grant that their heart be thus for them. God Himself longs that the hearts of Israel continue to fear Him all the days, because this does not depend on His decree but on their deeds.
in the essence of his birth. By the nature of his creation.
the fools who gaze at the heavens. Those who study the stars and believe in the power of the constellations and their influence on people's characters.
how could He command, etc.. For if the matter were not left to choice, there would be no purpose in the commandments of the Torah.
shall not the Judge of all the earth do justice. If people were not responsible for their deeds, how could a trial take place, with punishment or reward for fulfilling or neglecting the commandments.
whatever the Lord desired He did in heaven and on earth. If so, everything that happens is by God's will.
that everything is done by His will, etc.. Everything is done by His will, for He willed that choice be in our hands, as will be explained below.
and the sphere revolves in a circle. The system of spheres around the earth (see Hilchot Yesodei ha-Torah, chapter 3).
this has come to you from your own hand. The punishments you received came upon you from your own hands.
but does not the Holy One, blessed be He, know everything that will be before it happens. If so, how can there be free choice?
longer than the earth in measure and broader than the sea, etc.. The explanation of the matter is long and complex.
we already explained in the second chapter of Hilchot Yesodei ha-Torah. Halakhot 9-10.
He does not know with a knowledge that is external to Him. In relation to things that exist outside Him, like the knowledge of people.
to grasp this matter fully. To understand this matter completely, for there is no way to compare it to anything familiar.
the truth of the Creator. The existence of the Creator.
for man shall not see Me and live. Seeing a thing brings clear knowledge of its existence.
for My thoughts are not your thoughts. The Creator's thoughts do not work in the same way as those of creatures (see Hilchot Yesodei ha-Torah 1:10).
that a person's deeds are in the person's hand. As stated above.
the received religion. The tradition of the Sages.
but with clear proofs from the words of wisdom. That the matter is reasonable according to the intellect, as stated above in halakhah 4.
that appear to contradict this principle. Which was mentioned in the previous chapter, about the free choice a person has between good and evil.
and most people stumble over them. In understanding the meaning of those verses.
a great principle. A fundamental principle.
as a shield. A protection.
that prevent repentance from him. Block the way before him (see above, chapter 4).
make the heart of this people fat... and it will return and be healed. Israel's punishment is that its heart, ears and eyes will be closed, so that it does not repent and receive atonement.
that they were obligated to have repentance withheld from them. That this was their punishment.
and I will harden Pharaoh's heart. That the possibility of choice to agree to send Israel out of Egypt would be taken from him.
and you and your servants, I know. "That you do not yet fear the Lord God," from which it follows that his ability to choose had been taken from him in advance.

but for this reason. "I have raised you up, to show you My power, and so that My name may be declared throughout all the earth." That Moses' mission was meant to publicize this very matter, of removing the right of choice from one who is unworthy of it.
and likewise Sihon. The king of Heshbon in Transjordan, who refused Moses our teacher's request to let Israel pass through his land on their way to the land of Canaan.
and likewise the Canaanites according to their abominations. See Leviticus 18:3 and ibid. 27-28.
and they became liable. They were punished.
to help them on the path of truth. To assist them to walk the right way.
from which I will know Your ways and the unity of Your name. For it is "the foundation of foundations and the pillar of the sciences" (Hilchot Yesodei ha-Torah 1:1-6).
and what is this... therefore He instructs sinners in the way. If repentance depends on a person's choice, in what way is God's kindness expressed, in guiding and teaching sinners the way?
strength to learn and understand. Ability and desire.
and they will enslave them and oppress them. God told Abraham that his descendants would be strangers in Egypt for a long time, and that they would be enslaved by them.
and this people will rise up and go astray. God told Moses that after his death Israel would worship idols.
and why does He punish them. Did He not decree from the outset that they would behave this way!
that known person. A particular person.

for the needy shall never cease from the midst of the land. The statement of Scripture that there will always be poor people in Israel is not a decree on a particular person to be so, but a report of reality.
the oppressors and the evildoers. Those who harass and do evil.
and we have already said. Above 5:5.
that a person has no power to know, etc.. A person cannot understand how to distinguish between a general knowledge of what will be and a decree about the conduct of a particular individual.
as we have explained. Above, chapters 5-6.
and to shake off his hands. To abandon.
so that he dies a penitent. For a person's deeds are weighed at the time of his death (above 3:3; and see ibid., halakhah 6).
at his hour. Immediately, on that very day.
and he is found standing in his sins. Without repentance.
at all times let your garments be white. This means that the time for repentance is at all times.
in bad traits. Character traits and behaviors that are not corrected (see Hilchot De'ot 2:1).
frivolity. Much laughter.
to separate. To keep apart from them.
his thoughts. These are the despicable character traits.
imagine. Think.
that they subdue their inclination more than they do. Penitents master their inclination more than the righteous.
commanded about repentance. Called on Israel to repent (see above 4:2, 5:4, 6:5).
only through repentance. After they repent.
when all these things come upon you. The curses stated in the passage of rebuke.
and the Lord your God will return your captivity. He will gather Israel from all places.
and to Him you shall cleave. This is drawing near to the Divine Presence.
hated. Detested.
that in the language in which the Holy One, blessed be He, distances, etc.. The same expressions that were used against sinners are used regarding those who repent.
Jeconiah. A king of Judah at the end of the First Temple period, who did evil in the eyes of the Lord and was exiled to Babylon by Nebuchadnezzar (II Kings 24:8-15).
and they throw them in his face. They hurl them at him, as something not needed.
who asked this of your hand, to trample My courts... who among you, etc.. God has no desire for sinners to come to the Temple.
add your burnt offerings to your sacrifices and eat meat. God has no interest in your burnt offerings, and it is better that you eat them yourselves, as ordinary sacrifices.
let them not feel them. Not be offended by those words.
greater. Larger.
